cohort: The study included 136,519 women (who were either pregnant, in labor, or postpartum for up to 42 days) admitted to the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Teaching Hospital in Kerbala, Iraq, with 18,791 delivering.
finding: The implementation of the maternity dashboard resulted in significant improvements in maternal and neonatal care quality indicators, including an increase in normal vaginal delivery rates, a decrease in caesarean section rates, reduced stillbirths, fewer NICU admissions, and a reduction in early neonatal deaths.
mod_finding: The normal vaginal delivery rate increased from 66% to 68%, and the caesarean section rate decreased from 33% to 31% after the implementation of the maternity dashboard.
